connection_acceptance_requirement.rule: a stream must not be marked HEALTHY on TCP/WebSocket connect alone
required_sequence: first valid payload received within a bounded timeout
connection_acceptance_requirement.pre_healthy_state: STREAM_NOT_READY -- used whenever the first valid payload has not yet arrived within the bounded timeout

supervisor_authority_note: EvidenceHunter_collector_supervisor.py's state machine (CONNECTING -> STREAM_NOT_READY -> HEALTHY -> STALE -> RECONNECTING -> RESYNCING -> HEALTHY) is the sole project-level authority for component lifecycle and recovery. websocket-client's own built-in reconnect facilities (e.g. run_forever(reconnect=...)) must not be relied on as a second, independently-acting recovery mechanism running alongside the Supervisor; the low-level WS wrapper must use a mode where reconnect/retry decisions are driven explicitly by the Supervisor, not by the library internally.
force_order_semantics_note: forceOrder is implemented as approved (schema independently confirmed against the primary docs page). Its official semantics are a windowed snapshot/update-frequency push (at most one message per symbol per ~1000ms window, representing the latest liquidation order in that window), not a guaranteed complete per-event liquidation stream. Raw payload persistence and provenance/documentation for this stream must state this explicitly; the collector and any future research layer must never treat the absence of a forceOrder message as proof that no liquidation occurred in that window.
mark_price_status: DEFER_WITHOUT_BLOCKING_CORE_DATASET -- WS field-level schema for markPriceUpdate could not be cleanly verified from the primary docs page despite repeated attempts (only indirectly corroborated via REST premiumIndex fields and a third-party-adjacent official SDK repo, which PROJECT_OWNER/GPT ruled insufficient to implement against). Not implemented this changeset; the /market route reservation for it is documented but no markPrice stream code is written.
